# Rapier

> A free Markdown editor that a person and an agent edit together, live, with no account. The agent changes exactly the passage or drawing it read; the person's typing comes first, and they keep, drop or undo each change. The whole editor and its document fit in one offline HTML file, and pictures, editable drawings and layout travel inside one `.md` file that every Markdown app can read.

Connect an MCP client to `https://mcp.rapier.website/mcp` (streamable HTTP, no account or key) and call `rapier.open`. `rapier.guide` returns the full usage guide.

## What only Rapier does

- **One live document, two authors.** `rapier.open` returns `editor_url`, the editor in the person's browser. Each read (`document.get_context`, `document.get_outline`, `document.find`, `document.read_context`) returns a handle for exactly the text it disclosed, and `document.apply_edits` changes only that text. The person's typing wins; they choose FREE, CHECK or ASK; `document.undo_agent_change` reverses an agent change and keeps their later edits.
- **Diagrams the person can move.** `document.draw` turns `figures`, for example `[{"kind":"rect","label":"Ask"},{"kind":"rect","label":"Answer"},{"kind":"arrow","from":"Ask","to":"Answer"}]`, into a native SVG drawing with automatic layout and attached arrows. The person drags the shapes; the agent reads the changed drawing and revises it. The same tool paints with brushes and watercolour. Mermaid flowcharts render offline and stay text.
- **The whole editor in one file.** `npx rapier-html notes.md` writes `notes.rapier.html`: the editor with the document inside, offline, no account. `--propose original.md` opens it on the diff; `--return <url> --return-expires-at <time>`, from `document.create_return`, adds Send back.
- **Self-contained Markdown.** Pictures (new rasters as JPEG XL from Rapier's own encoder), drawings, layout and colour live inside one `.md` file. Everything beyond CommonMark and GFM is an HTML comment or a reference definition that other apps ignore.
- **Will/1.** `<!-- will/1 keep -->` and `<!-- /will -->` mark a region an agent must leave alone; `append` allows additions at its end, `edit` allows any change. Rapier enforces it on every agent edit.
- **Every format out.** `document.export` writes `markdown` (the exact source), `html` (the offline editor), `txt`, `page` (a rendered web page), `docx` and `pdf` (with the source attached).
- **An editor or a reader inside any app.** `npm install rapier-embed` frames the document editor or the read-only reader; the app keeps the document and its storage. `agent: true` gives the app's own agent the same tools through WebMCP.

## Connect

- MCP: `https://mcp.rapier.website/mcp`, with or without OAuth. `https://mcp.rapier.website/muse` admits OAuth hosts only and carries no embedded editor. Registry name: `io.github.jackskip22/rapier`.
- Claude Code: `claude plugin marketplace add jackskip22/rapier-plugins && claude plugin install rapier@rapier`.
- ChatGPT: the Rapier app opens a workspace in the conversation, from the sidebar, or on a `.md` or `.txt` attachment.
- In the page: the same tools on `document.modelContext` in browsers with WebMCP, and `window.RapierAgentBrowser.invoke(name, input)`.

## Builds

Each build is one HTML file that runs offline with no server.

- `rapier.html`: the whole app: editor, Draw, Paint, Water, Notes and the JPEG XL encoder. Give it to people.
- `rapier-document.html`: the editor without Draw, Paint, Notes and the encoder. Embed it where people edit; `document.draw` diagrams still work through the agent tools.
- `rapier-reader.html`: read-only, with search (words inside pictures included), the outline, reading settings, the fast-scroll circle, read aloud, copy, share, text export and print; no editing and no agent tools. Restyle it with `--rapier-*` properties and your own fonts. Its plug-ins (maths, diagrams, flowcharts, and Word and PDF files opened as Markdown) download when a document needs them, or come only from a directory on your origin that you name with `plugins`.

To keep the reader and its plug-ins in your codebase, download `rapier-reader.html`, fetch the plug-ins (`npx rapier-embed plugins ./public/rapier` verifies every file `rapier-plugins.json` lists; the manifest also stands at `https://rapier.website/embed/<version>/rapier-plugins.json`), and mount your copy:

```js
import {Rapier} from 'rapier-embed';
const reader = Rapier.mount(element, {build: 'reader', src: '/rapier/rapier-reader.html', plugins: '/rapier/', load: {content, filename: 'brief.md', revision: 1}});
```

## Docs

- [Agent guide](https://rapier.website/agents): workflows, every tool's behaviour and limits.
- [Tool catalog](https://rapier.website/AGENT-TOOLS.json): each tool's schema and effect.
- [Embedding](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/blob/main/npm/rapier-embed/README.md): the three builds, `Rapier.mount`, styling and plug-ins; the [embed contract](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier/blob/main/docs/embed-contract.md) is the wire protocol.
- [Self-contained Markdown](https://rapier.website/markdown-standard): the file format.
- [Will/1](https://rapier.website/will): the region standard, with a reference reader and a GitHub check.
- [rapier-markdown-kit](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-plugins/blob/main/npm/rapier-markdown-kit/README.md): read, write and render the format without the editor (MIT).
- [rapier-jxl](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier-jxl): the JPEG XL encoder (MIT).
- [Source](https://github.com/jackskip22/rapier): the builds and their source (AGPL-3.0-only).
- [Everything in one file](https://rapier.website/llms-full.txt): the public documents in full.

## Optional

- [Notes](https://rapier.website/notes): Markdown notes; agents use `notes.list`, `notes.read`, `notes.history`, `notes.set`, `notes.propose` and `notes.sync` on the store the host configured.
- [Draw](https://rapier.website/draw) and [Watercolor](https://rapier.website/watercolor): the canvas on its own.
- Hosted workspaces expire after 30 idle days; export links last 24 hours. Downloaded files stay independent.
